section: Solid waste, plastic waste, e-waste, biomedical and construction waste - rules and management
subsections: Hazardous chemicals in consumer products - PFAS, mercury lamps
Hazardous waste disposal - secure landfills, treatment, inventory

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes PFAS, often referred to as “forever chemicals”?
o: They are biodegradable chemicals used exclusively in cement production
They persist in the environment, occur in products such as food packaging, and may accumulate in animal bodies
They rapidly decompose in soil and water and do not accumulate in organisms
They are radioactive substances used mainly in fluorescent lamps
accepted.x: PFAS are persistent chemicals found in drinking water, food and food packaging. They do not break down easily and can accumulate in animal bodies.
accepted.tq: Use the option that combines the defining properties and common exposure pathways.
accepted.sec: Hazardous chemicals in consumer products - PFAS, mercury lamps

accepted.s:
With reference to PFAS, consider the following statements:
1. PFAS are widespread in drinking water, food and food packaging.
2. PFAS do not break down easily in the environment.
3. PFAS have been listed under the Stockholm Convention.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. PFAS are persistent contaminants found in several consumer exposure pathways and are now listed under the Stockholm Convention.
accepted.tq: Check each statement independently before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Hazardous chemicals in consumer products - PFAS, mercury lamps

accepted.s: Fluorescent lamps and compact fluorescent lamps are treated as household hazardous waste primarily because they contain:
o: Lead compounds
Mercury
Asbestos fibres
Polychlorinated biphenyls
accepted.x: Fluorescent lamps and CFLs contain mercury. When broken, they can release mercury vapour into the surroundings.
accepted.tq: Identify the hazardous constituent associated with the specific consumer product.
accepted.sec: Hazardous chemicals in consumer products - PFAS, mercury lamps

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the legal control associated with mercury-added products?
o: They are exempt from international environmental agreements
They are being phased out under the Minamata Convention
They are being promoted under the Stockholm Convention
They are regulated exclusively under the Basel Convention
accepted.x: Mercury-added products are being phased out under the Minamata Convention, which addresses mercury pollution and its risks.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between international conventions by matching the pollutant with the correct treaty.
accepted.sec: Hazardous chemicals in consumer products - PFAS, mercury lamps

accepted.s: Which of the following is an example of construction and demolition waste that is generally regarded as mostly inert?
o: Mercury vapour and fluorescent lamp powder
Concrete, bricks, dirt, rocks and debris
Used syringes, blood-soaked cotton and pathological waste
Pesticide residues and solvent sludge
accepted.x: Construction and demolition waste is mostly inert and commonly consists of concrete, bricks, dirt, rocks and debris.
accepted.tq: Select the option containing the characteristic material group rather than hazardous waste categories.

accepted.s: Approximately how much construction and demolition waste is generated annually, as indicated for India?
o: 1,200 million tonnes
1.2 million tonnes
12 million tonnes
120 million tonnes
accepted.x: Construction and demolition waste generation is indicated to be about 12 million tonnes per year.
accepted.tq: Use scale comparison to distinguish the stated annual quantity from tenfold alternatives.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a recognised reuse of construction and demolition waste?
o: Reprocessing for construction applications
Manufacture of bricks and tiles
Production of recycled aggregates
Use as a substitute for all hazardous chemical treatment
accepted.x: C&D waste can be reused as recycled aggregates and in bricks and tiles. It is not a substitute for hazardous chemical treatment.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the stated reuse pathway by separating construction applications from hazardous-waste treatment.

accepted.s: The Burari facility in Delhi is notable as:
o: India’s first mercury-recovery plant
India’s first fly-ash-based thermal power plant
India’s first secure landfill for hazardous waste
India’s first construction and demolition waste recycling plant
accepted.x: Delhi’s Burari plant is recognised as India’s first construction and demolition waste recycling plant.
accepted.tq: Match the named place with its distinctive facility rather than a neighbouring waste-management activity.

accepted.s: Under the Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016, which of the following activities falls within the scope of construction and demolition waste management?
o: Only construction of residential buildings
Building, renovation, excavation, road, flyover, bridge and pipeline work
Only mining and mineral processing
Only municipal household waste collection
accepted.x: The 2016 Rules cover waste arising from building, renovation, excavation, road, flyover, bridge and pipeline activities.
accepted.tq: Prefer the comprehensive scope when the rule covers multiple related activities.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Construction and Demolition Waste Management Rules, 2016:
1. The Rules provide for collection, transport, storage and re-processing of C&D waste.
2. Bulk generators may be subject to charges.
3. Construction and demolition waste is treated as a resource.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: The 2016 framework covers collection, transport, storage and re-processing, permits charges on bulk generators and treats C&D waste as a resource.
accepted.tq: Test the rule through its management stages, economic provision and resource-oriented approach.

accepted.s: Which new framework is associated with the Environment (Construction and Demolition Waste Management) Rules, 2025?
o: Polluter immunity for bulk generators
Extended Producer Responsibility for C&D waste
A national prohibition on using recycled aggregates
A complete ban on recycling construction waste
accepted.x: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has notified an Extended Producer Responsibility framework for C&D waste under the 2025 rules.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy instrument directly linked with the newer rules.

accepted.s: The Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016 replaced which earlier rules?
o: The Hazardous Wastes (Management, Handling and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2008
The Biomedical Waste Rules, 1998
The Municipal Solid Waste Rules, 2000
The Hazardous Wastes Rules, 1989
accepted.x: The 2016 Hazardous and Other Wastes Rules replaced the 2008 Rules.
accepted.tq: Separate closely related rule years by identifying the earlier framework that was replaced.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states a feature of the Hazardous and Other Wastes (Management and Transboundary Movement) Rules, 2016?
o: Import of hazardous waste for disposal is prohibited, and prevention is preferred over disposal
The Rules deal only with municipal biodegradable waste
The Rules prohibit all forms of recycling and co-processing
Hazardous waste may be imported freely for disposal without prior approval
accepted.x: The framework bans import of hazardous waste for disposal and follows a hierarchy in which prevention precedes safe disposal.
accepted.tq: Apply the waste-management hierarchy and identify the option consistent with both controls.

accepted.s: In the context of transboundary movement of hazardous waste, PIC refers to:
o: Public Inventory Certification
Pollution Impact Calculation
Permitted Industrial Conversion
Prior Informed Consent
accepted.x: PIC means Prior Informed Consent, a control associated with the import and export of hazardous waste.
accepted.tq: Break the abbreviation into its regulatory meaning before evaluating the options.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MSIHC Rules, 1989 — manufacture, storage and import of hazardous chemicals
CAEPPR Rules, 1996 — insurance compensation without fault
Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 — constitution of crisis groups
Contaminated Sites Rules, 2025 — regulation of fluorescent lamp manufacture
accepted.x: The MSIHC Rules, 1989 address the manufacture, storage and import of hazardous chemicals. CAEPPR concerns crisis groups, while the Public Liability Insurance Act provides no-fault relief.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair and reject options that swap the functions of neighbouring legal instruments.

accepted.s: The CAEPPR Rules, 1996 provide for the establishment of:
o: Only District Pollution Control Boards
International hazardous-waste tribunals
Only Central Crisis Groups
Central, State, District and Local Crisis Groups
accepted.x: The CAEPPR Rules, 1996 provide for Central, State, District and Local Crisis Groups for preparedness and response to chemical emergencies.
accepted.tq: Read the composition literally and avoid dropping the lower administrative levels.

accepted.s: The principal purpose of the Public Liability Insurance Act, 1991 is to provide:
o: Compensation only after criminal conviction of the polluter
No-fault insurance cover and immediate relief to victims of hazardous-substance accidents
Insurance exclusively for transport of municipal waste
Long-term subsidies to industries using fly ash
accepted.x: The Act provides no-fault insurance cover intended to give immediate relief to victims of accidents involving hazardous substances.
accepted.tq: Identify the legal purpose by focusing on the beneficiary, liability basis and timing of relief.

accepted.s: Under the Contaminated Sites Rules, 2025, which sequence correctly represents the time limits for assessment by the State Pollution Control Board?
o: Preliminary assessment in 30 days followed by a detailed survey in 60 days
Preliminary assessment in 90 days followed by a detailed survey in the next 90 days
Preliminary assessment in 180 days followed by a detailed survey in 30 days
Both preliminary assessment and detailed survey within 15 days
accepted.x: The SPCB is required to undertake a preliminary assessment within 90 days and a detailed survey in the subsequent 90 days.
accepted.tq: Track the sequential time periods and distinguish the first assessment from the follow-up survey.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Contaminated Sites Rules, 2025 is correct?
o: District reports on suspected contaminated sites are prepared half-yearly, and the framework covers 189 hazardous chemicals
The Rules cover only radioactive substances and require monthly reports
District reports on suspected contaminated sites are prepared annually
The Rules apply only to municipal dumping grounds and cover 89 chemicals
accepted.x: The framework requires district half-yearly reports on suspected contaminated sites and identifies 189 hazardous chemicals.
accepted.tq: Combine the reporting frequency with the stated chemical count and reject altered figures.

accepted.s: The Fly Ash Utilisation Notification requires fly ash to be used for bricks, cement and road construction within what distance of thermal power plants?
o: 50 km
100 km
300 km
500 km
accepted.x: The notification requires utilisation of fly ash for specified construction purposes within 300 km of thermal plants, helping prevent dumping on soil.
accepted.tq: Use the distance-based regulatory limit and distinguish it from nearer or broader alternatives.

accepted.s: Which of the following is a recognised use of fly ash in construction?
o: Treating hazardous waste without any further processing
Replacing all aggregates in every type of concrete
Making building bricks and partly replacing Portland cement in concrete
Manufacturing mercury lamps exclusively
accepted.x: Fly ash can be used to make building bricks and can partly replace Portland cement in concrete.
accepted.tq: Select the option that states practical uses without introducing an absolute or exclusive claim.

accepted.s: Which principle best describes the preferred approach to hazardous-waste disposal?
o: Landfilling is the first and preferred option for all hazardous waste
Hazardous waste should always be burned in open areas
Landfill is the last resort, while co-processing in cement plants and waste exchange are preferred where suitable
All hazardous waste must be discharged into surface water after dilution
accepted.x: Landfill is considered the last resort. APPCB prefers suitable co-processing as fuel in cement plants and exchange of waste between industries.
accepted.tq: Apply the waste hierarchy and reject options based on absolute or environmentally unsafe practices.
accepted.sec: Hazardous waste disposal - secure landfills, treatment, inventory

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes hazardous-waste management infrastructure in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Two CHWTSDFs, twelve pre-processing facilities and six permitted cement units
Six CHWTSDFs, two pre-processing facilities and twelve permitted cement units
Twelve CHWTSDFs, six pre-processing facilities and two permitted cement units
Two CHWTSDFs, six pre-processing facilities and twelve permitted cement units for co-processing
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh has two Common Hazardous Waste Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facilities, six pre-processing facilities and twelve cement units permitted for co-processing.
accepted.tq: Split the numerical options into infrastructure categories and match each figure to its correct category.
accepted.sec: Hazardous waste disposal - secure landfills, treatment, inventory

accepted.s: The two Common Hazardous Waste Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facilities (CHWTSDFs) in Andhra Pradesh are located at:
o: Guntur and Kadapa
Anakapalli and SPSR Nellore
Vijayawada and Kurnool
Visakhapatnam and Tirupati
accepted.x: The two CHWTSDFs identified for Andhra Pradesh are located in Anakapalli and SPSR Nellore.
accepted.tq: Use location-based recall and distinguish the named facility sites from other Andhra Pradesh cities.
accepted.sec: Hazardous waste disposal - secure landfills, treatment, inventory

accepted.s: Which system is used by APEMC for tracking hazardous-waste movement in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Satellite television monitoring
Biometric tracking of every waste container
Manual colour coding only
GPS tracking
accepted.x: APEMC uses GPS tracking for monitoring hazardous-waste movement and management.
accepted.tq: Match the institution with the specific monitoring technology stated for it.
accepted.sec: Hazardous waste disposal - secure landfills, treatment, inventory
